approach: Add `check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs after `check_code_survey`, plus one `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request));` line after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));` in `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3138). It applies when the reading has a capability and no question, the class is `code` or `tests`, at least one criterion is Behavior (the `check_code_survey` precondition, 3454-3461), and the request, with steward template lines removed, is a wrong-output report. Round 3 widens "wrong-output report" to the wanted-content wording the class actually has: a line with a content verb (list, show, display, include, contain, publish) plus `only`, `no longer`, `still` or `anymore` plus an output noun (page, listing, table, view, dashboard, site), unless the line has a creation word (add, create, new, introduce, implement). It also matches error words (wrong, incorrect, stale, broken, bug, regression) and fix/fixes/fixed/fixing with an output noun on the same line. When it applies, the reading needs (a) a criterion that says `root cause` and holds a location token (path, `::`, `()` or an `_` identifier) and a reason word (because, why, since), and (b) one Behavior criterion that names a test, a real-data word and a failure on the base. The error names each missing part with fixed phrases. Unit tests, corpus cases, one reader rule line and one CHANGELOG entry follow. The reader prompt, the pipeline and the records are not touched.

decisions.choice: Fix at the reading gate, as a new `step!` in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: Both jobs were accepted because the gate did not require a diagnosis. The gate runs on every reading with no model call, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case. The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom (budget reader 1997 of 2000, docs/system-facts.md) and is out of scope.

rejected.why: Out of scope, no headroom, not enforced.
One instance of the class; dropped by the brief.

rejected.option: Run new tests on a scratch copy of the base in the pipeline
rejected.why: A pipeline change, left for a separate job. This job requires only that a criterion say the test fails on the base.

decisions.choice: Decide applicability from request text with three cue families (error words, fix plus output noun, wanted-content wording), after removing steward template lines. Do not add a mandatory `Bug fix:` declaration.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. The class is defined by requests that described wanted page content: HISTORY.txt:13 'Show only open, above-limit proposals on the decisions page'; CHANGELOG.md:375 'now lists only proposals that wait for the owner'; CHANGELOG.md:384 'no longer lists proposals that were approved or rejected'. Error words alone return Ok for that shape, so the wanted-content family is added and the corpus refuse case uses that wording with no error word in it. Template lines are removed because hestia.rs:406-434 builds every steward request as `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: {title}` plus `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, `Seen ...` and `Introspection ...` lines, and the bare words fix and failure would match every steward job. The creation-word exemption keeps `Add a page that shows only failed jobs` (a feature) out. Bare shows/lists are not cues on their own because feature requests use them.

rejected.option: Mandatory `Bug fix: yes|no` assumption, modelled on `Code survey:`
rejected.why: No stored reading has the line, so the replay (REPLAY_HOLD_PERCENT 10, reading.rs:3630) would count nearly every past code reading with a Behavior criterion as newly refused, far above the 12% in the accepted reading. An optional line adds no enforcement, because the miss is the reader not saying it.
Returns Ok for the wanted-content shape of the cited jobs.

rejected.option: Match fix and failure as bare whole words
rejected.why: Catches CI races, prompt gaps and every steward job.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must contain `root cause` (a hyphen read as a space), a location token and a reason word. A location token has `::`, `.rs`, `()`, an `_` between letters, or `/` with at least two slashes or a `.` extension (so `and/or` does not count). A reason word is the whole word because, why or since. The words where and enters are dropped. The doc comment says the check is a text floor and the verifier and critic judge the diagnosis.
decisions.reason: Finding 2. The earlier signal words let 'states the root cause and why it happened' pass with no named entry point. Requiring a code location forces the reader to name the file or function where wrong items enter. The copied steward bullet 'The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates' has no location token and no reason word, so the round-2 copy-removal helper is not needed and is dropped, which makes the check smaller.

rejected.why: A copied request bullet satisfies it.

rejected.option: Keep where/why/because/enters as the only signal

rejected.why: Fits only the filter bug of the decisions page.

decisions.choice: The test criterion is one Behavior criterion with a whole word test or tests, a data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual, captured, or a word starting reproduc), a word starting `fail` and the whole word `base`.
decisions.reason: Introspection 20261105-051344-q9fv records tests that also pass on the base. Naming the base-failing run in one criterion is the reading-level part in scope. `reproduc*` lets a bug with no stored data say how it is reproduced. Requiring all parts in one criterion stops them being spread over several.

rejected.option: Test word and data word only
rejected.why: Does not require a failure on the base.
A bug with no stored data could not pass.

decisions.choice: Require a Behavior criterion before the check applies, as `check_code_survey` does.

Helpers. `bug_report_lines(request)` drops lines whose trimmed text starts `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:`, `Failure class:`, `Cause:`, `Seen ` or `Introspection `, and returns the rest lowercased, line by line. `is_wrong_output_report` is true when some remaining line has (i) a whole word wrong, incorrect, incorrectly, stale, broken, bug, bugs or regression; (ii) a whole word fix, fixes, fixed or fixing and a whole output noun (page, output, report, listing, table, view, dashboard, site); or (iii) a content verb (list, lists, show, shows, display, displays, include, includes, contain, contains, publish, publishes), a restrictor (the word only, anymore or still, or the phrase no longer), an output noun other than output and report, and no creation word (add, adds, create, creates, new, introduce, implement). Use `has_phrase` for whole words.

`is_root_cause_criterion(text)` reads the normalised text with hyphens as spaces. It needs the phrase `root cause`, a location token (`::`, `.rs`, `()`, an `_` with a letter on each side, or a `/` token with two or more slashes or a `.`), and the whole word because, why or since. `is_base_failing_test_criterion(c)` needs kind Behavior, a whole word test or tests, a data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual, captured, reproduc*) and a `fail` word plus the whole word `base`. risks.risk: The replay of past readings may newly refuse more than 10% (an estimate, not measured). The wanted-content family widens the cues, and the brief's criteria declare no share (`replay_declaration` reads only criteria and out_of_scope).
risks.mitigation: The Behavior precondition, the template removal, the creation-word exemption and the noun requirement keep the cues narrow. The share is not measured and is left as an open question for the user, who can add `expected N% of newly refused readings` to a criterion.

risks.risk: A false refusal on a feature or process request that has a cue for another reason (a `stale lock file`, `shows only` on a page the request changes).
risks.mitigation: The cue lists are short and whole-word. The error says exactly what to write, and the reader is re-read once with the refusal. Corpus accept cases cover `fixture`, `prefix`, `retry on failure`, `Fix the directory crash` and a new page that lists only failed jobs.

risks.risk: A bug-fix reading with only content criteria skips the check.
risks.mitigation: Same gap as `check_code_survey`. It is stated in the doc comment, and the criteria-evidence rule and the new reader rule line push readings toward Behavior criteria. Closing it is a separate job.

risks.risk: Steward root-cause requests are exempt, because their template lines are removed before cues are matched.
risks.mitigation: Those requests already carry the root-cause bullet, and the gate covers user requests. The gap is stated in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The location-token test is too strict or too loose for a real diagnosis.
risks.mitigation: It is declared a text floor. The accept unit test covers a path-only location, a `()` token, an `::` token and an `_` identifier, and the error shows examples to write.

risks.risk: The new READING_RULES line breaks the 220-byte line limit or the section-size assertion in briefs.rs. The section is probably near 2200 bytes today, so 2400 is likely to be exceeded (an estimate).
risks.mitigation: Keep the rule text at 215 bytes or less, read the measured size from the failing assertion, and raise the limit only by that amount. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`.

risks.risk: A new corpus case trips another check first (`check_criteria_evidence` producer-report phrases, `check_boundary_and_repo_files`).
risks.mitigation: Build each from `base_reading` and change one field. Use the existing deliverable `docs/guide.md` and survey path `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`, both in `repo_files()`. Avoid the words producer's report in criteria.

demonstrations.method: The unit test builds `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])` and replaces the criteria with one Behavior criterion that has neither a root cause nor a base-failing real-data test. It calls `check_root_cause_criterion(&reading, "The decisions page lists proposals that were rejected, which is wrong")` and asserts the error holds `a criterion that names the root cause (where wrong items enter and why they are not excluded)` and `a criterion for a test built from real decided data that fails on the base`.
